title: Molecular and genetic atlas of gastric mucosa from individuals with pathogenic germline variants
summary:
Stomach cancer is a common and fatal disease. There are genetic risk factors for the development of stomach cancer, e.g. so-called germline mutations. In addition, infection with the bacterium Helicobacter pylori, which is found in the stomach of around 30% of the German population, is another risk factor. However, the exact mechanisms of gastric cancer development are poorly understood.

In this study, malignant changes in the stomach and their precursors are identified and characterized in individuals with germline mutations from the Familial Breast and Ovarian Cancer Center (FBREK Center) of the Charité in order to better understand mechanistic pathways in gastric carcinogenesis. 

Individuals diagnosed with gastric cancer or precursors in this study will be treated outside of this study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Indication for gastroscopy
- Study cohort: confirmed pathogenic germline variant (see above)
Exclusion criteria:
- Post gastrectomy
- Refusal of endoscopy
- Increased risk of bleeding when taking a biopsy (e.g. anticoagulation that cannot be paused or coagulation disorders) and possibly a greatly increased risk of sedation (e.g. terminal heart failure)
- Pregnancy
